title: Crestline - Dedicated Capacity Discovery
summary: Discovery focused on dedicated GPU capacity. Customer wants isolation for PII workloads, predictable latency for fraud detection models, and burst capacity during end-of-day batch scoring. Key concerns: SSO/KMS, audit logs, and cost tradeoffs between hosted and dedicated. Agreed next steps: pricing SKU, security package, schedule a throughput benchmark, and connect Crestline infra for VPC/VLAN details.
action_items: Samir to send dedicated capacity pricing and SKU sheet by 2026-11-24
Elena to share security whitepaper and SOC2 summary by 2026-11-25
Marco to provide sample traffic profile + tail latency SLOs by 2026-11-23
Liam to share network/VPC architecture and firewall constraints by 2026-11-26
next_steps: Redwood to provide dedicated pricing and security package
Schedule 1-hour benchmark with infra team (session to test 4xA100 equivalent) week of 2026-11-30
Agree pilot start date and success metrics (throughput, p99 latency, cost per 1M tokens)
transcript:
00:00 Samir (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intro, I'm Samir AE on the accounts team, with Elena our SE. 00:12 Priya (Crestline CTO): Hi all, Priya here. our main interest is dedicated capacity for some of our fraud models, we handle PII so isolation is a must. 00:26 Elena (Redwood SE): Great thanks, can you talk a bit about the workload? batch vs realtime, QPS, model sizes? 00:35 Marco (Head of ML): Mostly realtime scoring at checkout, plus an end-of-day batch rerank. Realtime is about 60 qps average right now, spikes to ~250 during peak, p99 latency target is 100ms for short prompts. We also run a 7B cust model and occasionally a 30B variant for tougher cases. 00:55 Liam (Infra): For infra constraints, we need VPC peering and can't route traffic over public internet for the models handling PII. Also strict egress rules and our firewall blocks unknown ports. 01:10 Samir: Got it. Dedicated would give you reserved GPUs and network isolation - we can provision in a VPC with customer-managed peering or offer an on-prem package if needed. 01:25 Dana (Security): We need to see KMS integration, audit logs, and SOC2 artifacts. Also encryption at rest for KV cache and logging retention policies. 01:36 Elena: We support KMS/HSM + TLS in transit, and we generate audit logs per request. I'll share the SOC2 summary after this call. 01:46 Marco: A question on bursting - sometimes our traffic spikes 4x for short windows. How does Redwood handle burst without overpaying for idle GPUs? 01:56 Elena: Two patterns - reserved capacity for baseline and a burst pool you can enable to scale above reserved. Policies let you prioritize latency or cost; e.g., keep low-latency pool warm and route overflow to cheaper batch or hosted fallbacks. 02:14 Priya: If we use hosted fallback, are we sending PII out to hosted cluster? that's a no go for the sensitive endpoints. 02:22 Samir: Correct, for PII you'll want dedicated-only routing - we can set policy so sensitive routes never hit hosted. Non-PII can use hosted as fallback to save cost. 02:33 Liam: About scaling - what autoscale mechanisms are there? can we do scheduled scale for known batch windows? 02:40 Elena: Yes, autoscale supports scheduled scaling and reactive rules (CPU/GPU utilization, queue depth). For very short spikes, we recommend a small warm buffer + burst-on-demand to a cross-customer pool but for PII you'll want dedicated burst nodes or pre-warmed extra capacity. 02:58 Marco: Can you quantify cost difference? like 4x reserved vs burst pricing? 03:05 Samir: I'll send SKU pricing, rough rule of thumb is reserved ~60-70% discount vs on-demand, burst pricing depends on capacity type (dedicated burst vs hosted) - I'll follow up with concrete numbers. 03:20 Dana: Audit trail question - do you log token-level content? would that violate our data retention policies? 03:28 Elena: We can configure logging at route level. For PII routes we recommend no token-level logs and only metadata + request IDs; we support customer-managed keying for stored artifacts. 03:42 Marco: Network - we use private subnets and require static egress IPs for whitelisting vendor endpoints. Can Redwood respect static egress or do we need NAT on our side? 03:53 Liam: follow-up, we can't accept new IP ranges without security review. 03:58 Samir: We can work with you; dedicated in-VPC often uses your egress. For our hosted we publish ranges but for dedicated we can peer and use your NAT. 04:10 Priya: On performance, curious about p99 tail behavior for sequence-length variability. 04:18 Elena: Our runtime selects kernels based on model shape + requested sequence lengths, and we do KV cache reuse to reduce latency on consecutive calls. For 7B you should see sub-100ms p50 and p99 depends on prompt size - we'll run a benchmark to show real numbers. 04:35 Marco: That benchmark is critical - can we run with our payloads and sample traffic? 04:40 Samir: Yes, we'll set up a throughput/burst benchmark with your infra team. suggested: 30-minute run covering baseline and spike patterns. 04:50 Priya: Timeline - we'd like a pilot in Dec, production H1 2027 ideally. success metrics: p99 <200ms, cost below current infra spend by 20%, and zero data egress for PII routes. 05:05 Elena: Sounds reasonable, we often do a 4-6 week pilot for dedicated. 05:12 Marco: Any lock-in concerns? if we pin to a model variant and later want to move to hosted, is that friction? 05:20 Samir: We expose same API across hosted/dedicated/private, model pinning and rollouts are supported; migration is mostly config and data policies. 05:30 Dana: Legal/procurement - we need standard terms + DPAs, plus any on-prem statements for air-gapped installs. 05:40 Samir: We'll loop legal and send template agreements. 05:45 Priya: Ok quick recap? 05:48 Samir: Recap - Redwood to send dedicated pricing and SKU, Elena to share security docs/SOC2, schedule benchmark week of 11/30 with Liam and Marco, Crestline to send traffic profiles and network diagrams. 06:05 Marco: thanks all. 06:07 End of recording

Note: transcription has occasional mis-hearings (e.g., 'KV cache' rendered as 'K V cache' in some spots) and speaker overlaps around 02:20-02:40 where two people talk over each other.
